Evidence boundary

Useful submissions contain names, dates, records, locations, transactions, source links, court references or specific contradictions that can be checked.

  • Documented evidence
  • Official allegations
  • Credible leads
  • Analytical inference

Do not send

Threats, illegal material, passwords, stolen credentials, private intimate content, graphic exploitation material, or anything that could identify or endanger a victim or minor.

Client-Side Encryption

PGP Secure Send.

The message and permitted attachments are encrypted inside your browser to the public key of matrixreprogrammed@proton.me. The intake Worker receives only armoured OpenPGP ciphertext.

⌾
Security boundary: PGP protects the content. It does not make you anonymous and does not erase browser, device, network or timing metadata. For extreme-risk disclosures, seek specialist source-protection advice before using any ordinary website.
Recipientmatrixreprogrammed@proton.meKey stateNot loadedFingerprintPending key verification
Encrypted before submission.
Optional and encrypted before submission.
Maximum two files and 650 KB combined. Files are embedded in the encrypted envelope.

OpenPGP.js is version-pinned. The public key is retrieved through the Matrix Reprogrammed Worker from Proton’s public-key service and checked for the intended Proton address before encryption.

Evidence Discipline

Signal classification.

Documented Evidence

Supported by an identifiable record, document or verifiable source.

Official Allegation

A claim made in court, government, regulatory or law-enforcement material.

Credible Lead

Specific and potentially useful, but not independently verified.

Analytical Inference

A conclusion drawn from multiple established facts or patterns.

Speculation

A theory requiring substantial further verification and clearly labelled as such.

Correction

Evidence intended to challenge, refine or correct existing site material.

Figures & Sources

Figures on this page

Checked: 25 June 2026

Numbers on this page are public-record leads. Crime, migration, sexual-offence, payout, death, and crisis figures must be tied to named official, court, police, parliamentary, regulator, or reputable source records before they are presented as settled.

Evidence standard

What counts as a usable figure?

Official statistics, court records, ministry releases, police datasets, parliamentary material, regulator data, or clearly named public reports. Nationality, foreign-born status, asylum status, immigration status, charge, suspect, conviction, and victim categories must not be mixed.

Document trail

Open the underlying record

When the figure matters, follow the document link, source file, court record, official release, PDF, book, or video. The visible page should help readers reach the underlying evidence fast.
